claim: LLM help (GPT-4o, three modes incl. Dorst nine-step) did not raise novelty or usefulness of expert-rated design problem frames versus working alone (N=280 of 456).
agent_test: Run our O8 on the 3 Shin design problems vs no-O8 at equal tokens; blind-rate novelty and usefulness; add equivalence test.

claim: Felt help from LLMs (CSI 61-65, all 'good') is not evidence of better frames; self-report and measured quality came apart.
agent_test: Log self-rated confidence vs blind-rated quality for O8 outputs.

claim: A rigid Dorst nine-step scaffold costs more time (28.35 vs 23.25 min manual) with no quality gain.
agent_test: Compare light single-step reframe vs full nine-step at equal tokens.

claim: Expertise moderates: reframing-literate users get more novel frames from LLMs (+12.54%, p=0.01); gap not closed by the LLM.
agent_test: Vary the quality of the instruction given to the agent (expert vs naive reframe prompt) at equal tokens.

claim: Abstracting to principles before answering (step-back) gives large gains on physics/chemistry/TimeQA but fixes 20.5% and breaks 11.9% of errors; remaining errors are >90% reasoning. On a 2026 model (Qwen3.5-27B) step-back sat below zero-shot CoT in one benchmark average (56.71 vs 59.79, table read from garbled text), and thoughts-of-principles did not cut anchoring in GPT-4/4o; 2025-26 reasoning models are untested for step-back itself.
agent_test: Step-back as a gated sub-step; measure net fixed minus broken at equal tokens.

claim: Model-written rephrasing of the question lifts GPT-4 on ambiguous tasks (avg 64.95 to 89.77) but helps weaker models little; task set partly built for ambiguity. Rewriting 30 hard narrative puzzles into formal maths lifted o3 56.7 to 73.3 (p=0.023) and DeepSeek-R1 50.0 to 63.3 (p=0.043), not equal-token; meaning-preserving renames cost only about 2 points on Putnam variants.
agent_test: Rephrase step on ambiguous vs clear items; check no loss on clear items.

claim: Intrinsic self-revision without external feedback does not help and can hurt (CSQA 75.8 to 41.8 on GPT-3.5); finding the error is the bottleneck (GPT-4 mistake location 39.8 to 52.9%), and in 8 reasoning models over 90% of reflections after the first answer only confirm it. Reframe-by-self-review needs a localised or external signal. Scope: reasoning tasks without outside feedback.
agent_test: Fire O8 only on a failure signal vs always; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Surface prompt/format changes alone move accuracy by up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B), so a gain from 'reframing' wording must be tested against format noise.
agent_test: Control arm with a meaning-preserving paraphrase of the baseline prompt.

claim: Hand-rewritten, decomposed, itemised instructions improved GPT-3 on 12 tasks (+12.5% few-shot, ROUGE-L 44 to 58); corrects 24% of errors, causes 4%.
agent_test: Itemised-instruction rewrite vs plain prompt on current models (old-model result may vanish).

claim: Situation puzzles needing a default-frame break are hard for LLMs (ChatGPT 53/63% vs human 92%) and fail under rewording; restart with compacted confirmed facts helped in 5 puzzles (2/3 to 4/1 wins, no statistics). Larger evidence on restating facts: repeating all known facts every turn closed about 15-20% of a 39% multi-turn loss (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, four tasks); partial recovery only.
agent_test: Restart with compacted confirmed facts after K failed probes; test on BRAINTEASER with current models.

claim: On clinical reframing, light task-fit prompting (DoT, 0.956 recognition) beat reasoning models; more output tokens hurt reframe generation. Outside the clinic: longer reasoning also hurt in distractor and familiar-framing tasks (inverse scaling, Claude Opus 4 and R1) and flipped the reading of 'some' and 'or' (GPT-5 -20.6 and -18.8 points); but gains from more reasoning on hard maths are well known, so the effect is task dependent.
agent_test: Check whether longer reasoning degrades O8 reframe quality at equal tokens.

claim: AI images raise design fixation on an example (GenAI +0.32, image search +0.27, N=60); exposure to a candidate frame can anchor. LLMs are also anchored by prompt hints (62 questions, 11 of 162 differences against the anchor; 22-61% of questions anchored across models), and ignore-the-hint instructions did not remove it. No test yet of a model anchoring on its own first frame.
agent_test: Show or hide first-generated frame; measure copying of its features.

claim: Insight reframing in humans is abrupt, hard step is reassembling, and hints help (34% solve alone, +11% after hint).
agent_test: Give a hint-style 'you may change X' signal when stuck; compare.

claim: Physical-interaction boost of matchstick insight failed conceptual replication (n=54,45,45).
agent_test: None; human-only boundary.

claim: Opposites-based prompting raises spatial insight success in three studies by one group, no pooled effect size.
agent_test: Add an 'invert each assumption' sub-step; test on insight items.

claim: LLM models show a framing effect (GPT-4 admit rate 0.375 vs 0.780 by wording); debiasing prompts help unevenly and one made the gap larger (-0.570).
agent_test: Present each item in two wordings; measure answer flip rate with and without O8.

claim: A Dorst-step prompt (steps 1-3, 6) gave more 'interesting' research answers than plain QA (29/189 vs 17/189), n=7, no statistics; useful answers split into reinforcing vs reorienting.
agent_test: Replicate with larger n and blind raters; contrast with Shin null.

claim: Self-selected task-level method composition (Self-Discover) beats CoT on many tasks (T4D 30 to 69 PaLM-2L) at 10-40x less compute than self-consistency.
agent_test: Pick-a-method step before solving vs fixed CoT.

claim: Reframing helps cheap, targeted, and benchmark-scored; open design with human raters shows null or mixed profile (AI rated higher on framing clarity 4.64 vs 2.94 but lower on innovation 3.40 vs 4.66, n=32).
agent_test: Score clarity and novelty separately; do not equate clearer frame with better frame.

claim: No controlled evidence yet that Dorst's nine-step model improves human frame quality. The Dorst and Cross 2001 base is a qualitative protocol study of 9 designers, one brief, no control (read via a third-party copy). Schon, Dorst books, Rittel were not opened.
agent_test: None; treat as conceptual.

claim: In reasoning models the first answer or first step dominates the result: a wrong first step lowers final accuracy about 40% (DS-R1-Qwen-7B 94.8 vs 28.5), and later reflection adds only 1.4-3.5% accuracy for 17-48% of tokens. Frame choice early matters more than review late.
agent_test: Sample several candidate frames before committing, prune cheaply; compare with late reframing at equal tokens.

claim: Prompted anchors pull LLMs (GPT-4, 4o, 3.5; reasoning models less) and chain of thought, ignore-the-hint and self-review do not fix it; showing opposing anchors together helps in part.
agent_test: Show competing frames side by side; do not rely on telling the agent to ignore the first frame.

claim: Agreement across runs is not correctness: in a ReAct agent study 21 of 94 questions were answer-consistent and wrong; a commitment prompt reduced run variability 28% vs a filler but did not raise accuracy.
agent_test: Do not use self-agreement alone as a 'frame is fine' signal; add an outside check.

claim: Approach-level (strategy) variety helps test-time scaling and training more than wording variety, and comparing self-made solving perspectives beat self-reflection (+7.2% vs -0.51% on maths, GPT-3.5/4, Llama-2); wording-only reframes are not reliably above zero-shot CoT.
agent_test: Single ablation: strategy-changing reframe vs paraphrase vs plain resample at equal tokens.

claim: Shin 2025's null was sized for medium effects; with about 62 vs 218 per group it rules out effects above about 0.45 SD but not small ones (TOST power 0.34 at +-0.3 SD, 0.74 at +-0.4, 0.93 at +-0.5). Group sizes inferred; no raw data.
agent_test: Need raw ratings or a new study sized for equivalence at a stated bound.

claim: A meaning-preserving surface change costs about 2 points on Putnam variants (median) while changing the setting with the same proof plan costs about 10 points (o3 51.5 to 38.6); carrying a plan into a changed setting is the weak spot.
agent_test: Paraphrase control size is about 2 points; a goal or setting change must re-derive the plan.

claim: Unrelated prompts can match zero-shot CoT and common reframing prompts (Qwen3.5-27B 7-benchmark average: spurious 73.24, PromptWizard 67.99, zero-shot CoT 59.79, Step-Back 56.71), so gains from reframing wording need a prompt-noise control.
agent_test: Add a same-length unrelated-prompt arm to every O8 test.

claim: Localising the failure matters more than the correction: with the true error location correction gains about +5 to +44 points, a random location loses up to about 16; premature thought switching in reasoning models costs accuracy (AIME2024 QwQ 38.3 to 44.1 when switching is penalised).
agent_test: Fire O8 on a localised failure after sustained effort on one line, not on a global doubt.

claim: On checkable brainteasers a content hint (the insight) helped o3, R1 and Gemini on the Math set (+3.2, +5.6 and +3.2 points) while a prompt discouraging brute force helped little (R1 +3.4, o3 0, Gemini -0.8).
agent_test: Make the reframe supply a content change (a different representation or goal), not a style rule.
